Audio Priority Bar 2.5.0 adds microphone mute, brief notices when automatic switching picks a device, and a Settings window rebuilt to look like System Settings. Upgrading from 2.4.0 needs no migration, and your existing priorities and overrides are kept.

## Microphone mute

- The top of the panel now has an output row and a microphone row. Click the round icon button to mute, and it turns red while muted. Drag the slider or scroll to set the level.
- Mute the microphone from the right-click menu, or by Option-clicking the menu bar icon.
- The mute follows automatic and manual switching to the next microphone, and follows mutes made in System Settings or on a headset.
- Microphones without a mute control are muted by setting their input level to zero. The level is restored when you unmute, when you quit, after a crash, or when an unplugged microphone returns.

## Notices

- A **Microphone muted** reminder appears below the menu bar icon when an app records while you are muted.
- When automatic switching picks a new device, a brief notice lists it with its icon and name. An output and a microphone switching together get one line each, and both halves of one headset share a single line.
- Each notice can be turned off in Settings.

## Settings and panel

- Settings is a grouped form with Startup, Devices, Notices and Updates sections, like System Settings, and each option explains itself underneath.
- While Open at Login waits for approval, Settings offers a button that opens Login Items, and the status clears once you approve.
- Checking for and downloading updates sit together with a progress indicator, and Quit moves to the About row.
- The automatic switching explanation sits under its switch and only appears when it adds something.
- The open panel no longer slides sideways when the menu bar icon changes width, and no longer shows a square outline around its rounded corners.

## Install

```bash
brew install --cask camguillory/tap/audio-priority-bar
```

Alternatively, download `AudioPriorityBar.zip` and `AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256` below into the same folder, verify the archive, and move the app to `/Applications`:

```bash
shasum -a 256 -c AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256
```

The release is universal for Apple silicon and Intel. It is ad-hoc signed, not signed with an Apple Developer ID or notarized. If macOS blocks the first launch, open **System Settings > Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway**.

Jabra Link monitoring may request Input Monitoring permission. Link 380 is hardware-verified. Link 390 is expected to work through the same capability check but remains unverified on hardware, and monitoring fails open when the link state cannot be read.
